stories.headline: Nvidia board reportedly weighs removing Jensen Huang as shares plunge

sources.body:
Peter Hoskins Business reporter, Singapore

If Jensen Huang is removed as the boss of Nvidia he won't be the first or last corporate leader to be ousted for having an affair.

But he would be the most high-profile and consequential CEO in recent history to meet such a downfall.

His company's computer chips power the data centres that drive AI and he has been a highly vocal advocate for the technology.

Variously known as "the Taylor Swift of Tech" and "Daddy Huang" in Taiwan – both his birthplace and the home of "Jensanity" – he is the face of the global AI boom.

Huang's fans are not just on the streets of Tapei but also include the man behind the Resolute Desk in the Oval Office, Donald Trump.

Just this week, the US President backed Huang despite reports that he had an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

What the board of Nvidia will now be wrestling with is whether Huang can carry on in his role as the firm's leader and, if not, who could replace him.
sources.headline: Nvidia's shares plunge as US tech giant's board reportedly weighs ousting CEO Jensen Huang

sources.body: Nvidia's board is meeting late Wednesday to consider removing chief executive Jensen Huang, as reports of two extramarital affairs and an investigation into alleged links to a Chinese spy fuel a market sell-off and raise questions about the chipmaker's leadership.
sources.headline: Nvidia board to decide whether to oust longtime CEO Jensen Huang

sources.body:
Chip giants stock price falls more than 8 percent amid speculation over co-founder’s position.

Chip giant Nvidia’s stock price has tumbled amid reports that its board of directors is meeting to consider the future of CEO Jensen Huang.

Nvidia shares fell 8.6 percent in after-hours trading on Wednesday as questions swirled over Huang’s position at the top of the $4.2 trillion company.

The plunge comes after The New York Times, The Wall Street Journal and the Financial Times reported that Nvidia’s board of directors would discuss Huang’s position over allegations that he engaged in an extramarital relationship with an Nvidia employee, in addition to an affair with a woman accused of working with Chinese intelligence services.

Nvidia, which launched an investigation into Huang on Sunday, did not immediately respond to Al Jazeera’s requests for comment.

Huang, who co-founded Nvidia in 1993, is one of the most visible faces of the artificial intelligence (AI) boom, spearheading the development of high-end graphics processing units used to train and run frontier models.

The leather jacket-sporting tech executive’s position has also placed him at the centre of the geopolitical rivalry between the United States and China, which are locked in a battle for supremacy in AI.

As a confidant of US President Donald Trump, Huang has lobbied for the easing of restrictions on exports of high-end chips to China, putting him at odds with national security hawks in Washington who argue that Beijing must be blocked from access to cutting-edge US tech.

If Nvidia’s board were to oust Huang, 63, it would mark a seismic moment for the chip giant.

Viewed as integral to Nvidia’s meteoric rise to the ranks of the world’s most valuable companies, Huang is known for a centralised leadership style that places him at the centre of the company’s day-to-day operations and strategic decisions.

“Jensen is Nvidia; without him, the company loses its central, animating spirit,” Jay Goldberg, a senior analyst at Seaport Research Partners in San Francisco, told Al Jazeera.

“The organisation is built around him and replacing him will be very painful organisationally, and impossible to do personality-wise.”

It is unclear whether Nvidia has a succession plan, and analysts see few obvious candidates to take Huang’s place.

Dan Ives, senior managing director at Yorkville Ives, said Huang has been the “hearts and lungs” of Nvidia and that investors will closely scrutinise the executive’s possible replacement.

“We believe Nvidia’s value is $300 per share with Jensen as CEO and $225 per share without Jensen as CEO,” Ives said in a note to clients, adding that the company would navigate the turmoil and “remain a core foundational piece of the AI Revolution.”

“Jensen is not replaceable by another CEO or group of interim executives, but Nvidia likely now has to move on without Jensen at the helm, which seemed like a Twilight Zone episode narrative before Sunday afternoon when the news broke,” Ives said.

Nvidia has been the focus of international intrigue over the past week amid reports that Huang had a relationship with a Chinese woman who US intelligence officials determined had been recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security.
sources.headline: Nvidia shares plunge amid reports board to discuss CEO Huang’s future

stories.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to prisoner exchange as US envoys prepare separate meetings with both leaders

sources.body: Kyiv and Moscow on Wednesday agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange as the final day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi came to an end, though neither side gave a concrete figure. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday.
sources.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap as peace talks end

sources.body: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow and Ukrainian leader Volodymyr Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday, seeking to build on two days of talks in Abu Dhabi. Zelensky said a window of opportunity could emerge to end the war before 2027, as Europe pushes for a role in negotiations. Follow our liveblog for the latest updates.
sources.headline: Live: US envoys to meet Putin and Zelensky after Abu Dhabi talks

sources.body:
US envoys to visit Moscow and Dublin on Thursday for talks with Vladimir Putin and Volodymyr Zelenskyy respectively

Russia and Ukraine have agreed to the “largest prisoner exchange” of the war at their first US-brokered talks since February but made little progress towards a broader peace agreement.

Both sides sent senior delegations to the two-day talks, led by Donald Trump’s envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff, in an effort to find a solution to end the nearly-five-year war.

David Arakhamia, a senior member of Ukraine’s delegation, said the Russian team had arrived with “very, very strict directives”, making it difficult to narrow differences. But he said there had been “really big progress” on security guarantees for Ukraine after the war. “I think we have good momentum to bring about a solution before the new year,” Arakhamia said.

Kushner, Trump’s son-in-law, also struck an upbeat tone, saying he could see a path to an agreement. “These deals are very hard and complex, and this one is very emotional, very complex. It’s a very hot war,” he said. “But we see all the different ingredients to make a deal. We just have to figure out how to refine those ingredients, organise them and create the right structure and pathway.”

Kushner said the planned exchange, expected to involve more than 1,000 prisoners from each side, would “reunite families, build trust and create momentum towards peace”.

The US envoys are due to travel to Moscow on Thursday to discuss the Abu Dhabi talks with Vladimir Putin, before heading to Dublin, where they are expected to meet Volodymyr Zelenskyy and a group of European partners.

“In close coordination with Ukraine and our European partners, we have aligned on proposals we will discuss with President Putin in Moscow tomorrow, followed by consultations with President Zelenskyy,” Kushner said.

But despite the optimism, Kushner also said the two sides had yet to resolve their territorial dispute.

Russia’s territorial demands have shifted over time, but Moscow has made clear it wants control of all the Donbas, including areas still held by Kyiv, as well as the parts of two southern regions it does not yet occupy.

Vladimir Medinsky, the hardline Russian official who led Moscow’s delegation, said that “every inch of our land will be returned to Russia, one way or another,” in a sign that Moscow was unwilling to soften its territorial demands. Russia would be satisfied with the negotiations only “when there is peace on its terms”, he added.

He also said the main task was to create a new security system in Europe that would become “a new Yalta and Potsdam”.

Medinsky said Europe’s post-second world war security system was failing, with Ukraine merely the place where its wider problems had erupted. “Essentially, the whole body is sick, and Ukraine was just a cyst that burst. The whole body must be cured. A Band-Aid won’t be enough,” Medinsky said.

His focus on Europe’s wider security order is likely to heighten concern among European leaders that Washington and Moscow could reach a broader agreement on the continent’s security, potentially limiting Nato’s military presence in eastern Europe. Russia appears to be seeking to revive demands it presented to Nato in 2021, including a halt to further enlargement that would rule out Ukraine’s membership, restrictions on Nato forces and weapons in European countries that joined after 1997, and limits on missile deployments.
sources.headline: Ukraine talks in Abu Dhabi bring progress on prisoners but not on peace

stories.headline: Iran threatens wider retaliation, including against US bases in Europe used for attacks

sources.body: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Wednesday that Tehran would attack US bases located in Europe if they were used to carry out bombing raids against the Islamic republic. The heavy defeat of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections earlier this month seems to have pushed Washington to pull back its threats to carry out fresh strikes against Iran.
sources.headline: Tehran will strike US bases in Europe if used to attack Iran, security chief says

sources.body:
Israeli security cabinet orders military to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, Israeli media reports.

Israel has reportedly ordered its military to step up readiness for possible strikes on Iran as Tehran warned it would expand the war beyond the region if attacked.

Israel’s security cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, has ordered the military to step up preparations for an attack on Iran, Israeli media reported on Wednesday evening.

“The directives issued by the security cabinet to the Israeli military could lead it to carry out activities that could trigger a war,” public broadcaster KAN reported.

KAN said the directives were made public after Israeli opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot issued a statement telling Netanyahu – who is serving as prime minister in a caretaker capacity – not to deploy the military “without a direct and immediate threat” until the next government is formed.

Eisenkot was offered the chance to form a new government by Israeli President Isaac Herzog over the weekend after Netanyahu’s ruling coalition lost its parliamentary majority in the October elections.

Netanyahu, who is on the cusp of losing power if the opposition succeeds in forming a government, has been adamant that the war on Iran will continue until the collapse of the government in Tehran.

Reports of Israeli preparations to attack Iran come at a time of intense diplomatic efforts to avert further conflict and reach a diplomatic solution.

US President Donald Trump has said that he is prepared to return to waging war if a diplomatic track offered by Qatar fails to facilitate a deal between Washington and Tehran.

Iran’s security chief Mohsen Rezaei said in a social media post, “If the US launches another war against Iran, every military base involved in the aggression, from West Asia to Europe, will be a legitimate target for Iran’s lethal strikes.”

“No safe distance. No safe haven. No immunity,” he added.

Al Jazeera’s Resul Serdar Atas, reporting from Tehran, said the Iranian leadership has been discussing whether or not to appoint the hawkish Rezaei as Iran’s new chief negotiator.

“In Tehran, there have been voices saying that if this status quo goes on for quite a long period of time, Iran will not wait and might take pre-emptive action,” Atas said, adding that the current lead negotiator, Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, has commented on Iran’s determination to move beyond this state of “no war, no peace” through “sustainable deterrence” if negotiations fail.

Ghalibaf told Al Jazeera in an exclusive interview published on Wednesday that the Strait of Hormuz will “never return” to its status prior to the US-Israel war on Iran and that “the ball is now in the American court”.

“What stands in the way of an agreement is our lack of trust in the United States,” he said.

In Washington, DC, Al Jazeera’s Alan Fisher said Trump is still justifying why he went to war with Iran and saying that it would end soon.

US Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also said the Trump administration’s economic pressure campaign against Iran is proving so effective that a resumption of large-scale military operations is unnecessary.
sources.headline: Iran warns of expanded retaliation as Israel reportedly readies to attack

sources.body:
Regime adviser says Tehran could be forced into pre-emptive strikes if stalemate continues

Senior Iranian officials believe the US is planning either further military strikes or an ever-tightening economic stranglehold that will push Tehran into retaliatory action.

The assessment comes from Mehdi Mohammadi, an adviser to Iran’s chief negotiator in talks with the US, Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf.

Mohammadi said on his Telegram channel that the Americans had proposed a timeframe of about two weeks after which Donald Trump would make a decision on military action. Mohammadi, who is regarded as a reliable indicator of Ghalibaf’s thinking, cast doubt on the US president’s claim that the military option was off the table . He claimed Washington was preparing for a limited strike and Iran was already preparing a response.

If the US sanctions continued, he said, a comprehensive pre-emptive war would be needed “to increase the cost of sanctions for the enemy”.

Mohammadi described the US response to Iran’s latest proposals on reopening the strait of Hormuz as “not only unsatisfactory but completely deceptive”. “They do not want to release the frozen funds,” he said. “They do not want to lift the sanctions and they do not want to stop the war in Lebanon.”

He also disclosed that Iran had rejected a request from the US vice-president, JD Vance, for a direct meeting with its negotiators before giving a response to Tehran’s conditions for lifting the siege on the strait.

For now, Trump has settled on a strategy of suffocating Iran through economic pressure and tightening the blockade on its oil exports while facilitating those of other Gulf states through Hormuz.

Mohammadi’s assessments suggest some senior Iranians fear Washington’s strategy might work by destabilising the country. The thinking goes that economic turmoil might spark street protests, potentially around the anniversary of nationwide demonstrations that began in late December last year.

On this basis, the Iranian leadership might conclude that the status quo – a “no peace, no war” impasse – was not sustainable and pre-emptive action was required.

Despite Iranian claims that their blockade of the strait is working, there is concern that Brent crude is at a relatively low $93 a barrel, while Saudi oil production is near prewar levels of 9.3m barrels a day. In an attempt to close any loopholes, Iran said it bombed a US radar post on the Omani island of Didamar three days ago.

In another development, Mohsen Rezaei, the secretary of Iran’s national security council, said he had told Russia that Iran was not prepared for even a particle of its highly enriched stockpile of uranium to leave the country, saying it might be needed for planned nuclear-powered submarines.

A third senior official, Mohammad Mokhber, an adviser to Mojtaba Khamenei, Iran’s supreme leader, warned Europe that any complicity in the US blockade would be “an act of war that will be etched in the nation’s historical memory”.

Tehran has been increasingly clear that US bases in Europe will be targeted if fighting resumes. Rezaei said: “If American planes take off from a distant military base and come to this country to bomb Iran, we will also target that base. We are announcing this now so they have no excuse tomorrow.”
sources.headline: Trump planning new military assault or tighter sanctions, say Iranian officials

stories.headline: Israeli strike on Gaza's Nasser Hospital kills at least six, civil defence agency says

sources.body:
At least six people have been killed after an Israeli airstrike hit a building at Nasser Hospital in southern Gaza, an official from the Hamas-run civil defence agency has said.

The strike hit the surgery department of the hospital in Khan Younis, wounding at least 20 people and causing extensive damage, spokesperson Mahmoud Basal told news agency AFP.

A surgeon is reported to be among those who were killed during the strike early on Thursday.

There has been no immediate response from the Israeli military. The BBC has contacted the Israel Defense Forces for comment.

The BBC is prevented by Israel from reporting independently from inside the Gaza Strip, and is unable to verify details of the incident.

Recovery work is carried out by the Civil Defence in Gaza, which operates under the Hamas-run interior ministry. Its efforts have been supported by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC).

Nasser Hospital, the largest in southern Gaza, was hit by a double Israeli strike in August 2025 , which killed at least 20 people, including journalists and health workers.

Israeli strikes on Gaza have continued despite a ceasefire agreement in October last year. More than 1,600 people have been killed since then, according to Gaza's Hamas-run health ministry, whose figures are considered reliable by the UN.

Israel and Hamas have accused each other of violating the ceasefire.

The humanitarian crisis in Gaza has also worsened from recent heavy rains that reportedly flooded tens of thousands of tents that were housing displaced families.

The Gaza war was triggered by the Hamas-led attack on southern Israel on 7 October 2023, when about 1,200 people were killed and 251 others were taken hostage.

Since then, more than 74,645 people have been killed in Gaza, the health ministry says.
sources.headline: Israeli strike on Nasser Hospital kills at least six, Gaza civil defence agency says

sources.body:
Nasser Medical Complex in Khan Younis attacked as UN appeals for urgent aid to deal with heavy rains in the enclave.

Israeli attacks have killed at least nine Palestinians across Gaza, as the United Nations made an emergency appeal for waterproof tents to shelter hundreds of thousands exposed to flooding due to heavy rains.

At least four Palestinians were killed in an Israeli air strike on the Nasser Medical Complex in western Khan Younis, southern Gaza in the early hours of Thursday, according to Gaza’s Civil Defence spokesperson Mahmoud Basal.

An Israeli air attack on Wednesday killed 38-year-old Mohammed Salem al-Daash in the al-Sabra neighbourhood, south of Gaza City.

Another Palestinian was shot and killed by Israeli forces east of the al-Bureij camp in central Gaza, and another was killed in an Israeli drone strike in the al-Nasr neighbourhood, northwest of Gaza City.

At least two Palestinians were killed and several others wounded in a strike targeting a tent sheltering displaced people in the Sheikh Radwan neighbourhood, north of Gaza City.

Al Jazeera’s Hind Khoudary, reporting from Gaza City, described the Israeli attacks as indiscriminate targeting of civilians, saying people who were carrying on with simple attempts to survive lost their lives, such as “a man filling up a water tank, [who] was killed in a drone strike”.

“In another attack, two brothers from the al-Absi family were killed while they were sheltering inside their tent on al-Jalaa Street,” she said, adding that nowhere in Gaza was safe.

The Israeli attacks came as the UN appealed for more tents to be sent to the enclave because at least 70,000 tents were flooded in weekend rains, according to Gaza’s Government Media Office.

Heavy rain has directly affected at least 106,000 people in Gaza in recent days, according to UNICEF, with thousands of tents for displaced Palestinians submerged under water and latrines overflowing into camps.

NGOs and local organisations say they do not have the resources or capacity to deal with the crisis, as Israel continues to restrict the entry of essential aid.

“Ultimately, we need the Israeli authorities to cooperate with giving the permissions so that we can bring those tents in,” UN deputy spokesperson Farhan Haq told reporters at a media briefing, adding that apart from funding, Israeli permits were needed “to get this in”.

Certain countries supporting aid deliveries to Gaza say that delivering winter supplies will have to wait for the formation of an Israeli government, said Tom Fletcher, the UN under-secretary-general for humanitarian affairs.

In a statement, Fletcher said foreign ministers have assured their support, “but also repeatedly said that progress would be hard until after Israeli elections. Now we’re told to wait for the formation of a government”.

“This is not an acceptable excuse,” he added, citing international law and the consequences of delays, blockages and funding cuts.

Italy’s Foreign Minister Antonio Tajani said on Wednesday that Rome has launched a new emergency initiative worth 5 million euros ($5.5m) to provide immediate assistance to the Gaza Strip following the flooding.
sources.headline: Israeli strikes hit medical complex as nine killed across Gaza

stories.headline: Hoax bomb threats trigger school evacuations across Italy and parts of the UK

sources.body:
Some 6,300 schools across Italy and more than 700 in Scotland and Northern Ireland have received bomb threats, according to local authorities.

In Italy a number of buildings were evacuated as a precaution but Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said checks so far had not indicated any evidence of "concrete danger".

"These reports appear rather linked to a strategy intended to cause alarm and concern," she said on Facebook.

Scotland's education secretary Mairi McAllan said there was no risk to the public and specialist cyber-crime officers were working to identify the source of the messages. In Northern Ireland education officials told schools to remain open unless otherwise advised by police.

It is unclear whether the incidents are connected.

"As a parent and as a constituency MSP I understand just how concerning this will be for parents, for pupils, for carers and for school staff," McAllan said.

Scottish police had earlier said that the warnings were "immediately assessed" as hoaxes. However some local authorities confirmed that some schools had been evacuated.

"Our advice is that there is no requirement to evacuate schools or keep children away from education based solely on the content of the emails," Police Scotland said.

Italian officials said a single email appeared to have been sent on Wednesday to the inboxes of 6,300 out of a total of 7,476 state schools, and private schools were unaffected.

The message, said to be from a certain "Mikhail Andropov, leader of Vilayat di Misoginistan", caused alarm in many schools.

The BBC has seen the email sent to Scottish schools which appeared to have similar wording, and also referenced the name Mikhail Andropov, although as leader of a "Red Owl" project.

Italy's Education Minister Giuseppe Valditara said the incidents involving Italian schools were probably a "cyber-attack, not a genuine risk", adding that there appeared to be a clear strategy behind the rash of threats in across Europe targeting flights, supermarkets and even hospitals.

Italian airports along with airlines elsewhere in Europe were hit by a series of bomb hoaxes last week that prompted a series of scares, evacuations and widespread disruption.

Although a number of threats were claimed by an extremist misogynistic group, it later denied any link to the false warnings.

On Wednesday one Milan headteacher, Anna Bertato, told Italian media she had checked the email address of the sender online: "It was already classified as spam by a student at a university in Taiwan."

Another Milan headteacher, Massimo Nunzio Barrella, told Adnkronos news agency that he had immediately realised the email was spam when it arrived in his inbox at 08:59 and he decided not to evacuate his school and reassured parents who phoned in.

"The text seemed almost comical," said Barrella, "it was like a message from Martians: 'We have come to annihilate you.' I even had a bit of a laugh."

Although many schools were initially evacuated on Wednesday, the alarm was quickly lifted, and pupils were allowed to return to class. Some parents decided to take their children home for the day, but the majority of schools in Milan did not send their pupils home.
sources.headline: Thousands of schools in Italy, Scotland and Northern Ireland hit by threats in suspected bomb hoax

sources.body: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland, which reportedly prompted some evacuations in Scotland. Meloni said she had called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs for Wednesday to discuss the threats. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
sources.headline: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats

sources.body:
Unos 6.300 centros escolares italianos han recibido este miércoles una falsa alerta de bomba , y unos 300 han sido evacuados , lo que ha provocado escenas de caos en varias ciudades del país , con miles de jóvenes en la calle, muchos preocupados. La amenaza llegó en un delirante correo electrónico enviado desde una dirección vinculada a una universidad de Taiwán. La prensa italiana ha difundido el texto íntegro y el supuesto nombre de su autor: un tal Mikhail Andropov, que se presenta como "líder del Vilayat de Misoginistan", una supuesta provincia de un califato que no existe .

"Hemos venido a aniquilaros. Perpetraremos un genocidio contra los italianos", se leía en el mensaje, que aseguraba además que en los centros había, dentro de una bolsa de plástico, un potente explosivo con detonador a distancia . "De vosotros solo quedarán huesos y una papilla sanguinolenta", continuaba, antes de añadir que también se había colocado una bomba en el motor del coche de la primera ministra y que después remataría a los supervivientes "a cuchilladas".

Tras conocerse la situación, que ha afectado ciudades como Roma, Milán, Nápoles y Bolonia , la primera ministra, Giorgia Meloni , ha reaccionado en Facebook. "Estos mensajes parecen responder a una estrategia dirigida a generar alarma y preocupación", ha dicho. Ha anunciado también un Consejo de Ministros urgente para coordinar la respuesta y ha añadido: "Por ahora, de las averiguaciones efectuadas, no emerge ningún elemento que haga pensar en un peligro concreto". El ministro de Defensa, Guido Crosetto , ha hablado de "una estrategia clara de terror", aunque también de posibles "mitómanos" que buscan llamar la atención, no necesariamente vinculados a países extranjeros.

Por su parte, el titular de Educación, Giuseppe Valditara , ha pedido calma . "Del contenido del correo electrónico se desprende claramente que el riesgo real es prácticamente inexistente", ha declarado, y ha señalado que lo más probable es que se trate de un ciberataque .

Es, en cualquier caso, la segunda vez en pocos días . A comienzos de noviembre, una cadena de mensajes similar, dirigida a más de 270 directores escolares , interrumpió las clases e hizo que la policía inspeccionara decenas de institutos en todo el país. Desde entonces, la policía mantiene abierta una investigación para rastrear el origen de los envíos e identificar a los autores. Como entonces, los controles policiales de esta vez no han hallado artefacto alguno ni indicios de un peligro real.

Se sabe aún muy poco del verdadero objetivo de estos ataques y de sus autores. Ningún Gobierno ha atribuido por el momento las amenazas , mientras que el apellido del supuesto autor coincide con el del descarado líder soviético Yuri Andrópov —jefe del KGB durante 15 años y en parte es un modelo para el propio presidente ruso, Vladímir Putin—, y es el mismo que firmaba el viernes pasado las alertas de bomba contra la televisión pública irlandesa RTÉ y la cadena búlgara Nova. Sin embargo, no hay pruebas sólidas de un vínculo concreto con el Kremlin , como también ha señalado la agencia de noticias Reuters.
sources.headline: Alarma en miles de escuelas de Italia, Irlanda del Norte y Escocia: mensajes delirantes y una cadena de falsas bombas

stories.headline: Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate seat in historic Democratic upset

sources.body: Mississippi voted blue, in a shock win for Democrats. Democrat Scott Colom ousted Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith in a state that went for President Donald Trump by 23 points in 2024. He will be the first Black senator elected in Mississippi since the Reconstruction era — and the first Democrat from the state headed to the Senate in 44 years. Colom, a Democratic district attorney, ran a scrappy campaign that saw some national money and resources in the final stretch of the race. Hyde-Smith was appointed to the Senate in 2018 and had since won election to the seat twice, but she faced attacks from Colom that she was out of touch and indifferent to rising grocery and gas prices during Trump’s second term. National Democratic groups hadn't paid much attention to the Mississippi Senate race until an October surge of excitement for Colom drew late spending and attention. Colom's win is a boost to the Democratic Party as it seeks to gain a larger foothold in the South and improve their standing with Black voters. It’s also a major vindication for Colom and other Southern Democrats who argued Mississippi had been neglected for far too long.
sources.headline: Mississippi elects Democrat Scott Colom to Senate in massive upset

sources.body:
Democrat Scott Colom has won the US Senate race in Mississippi, delivering a shock victory for the party in a deeply conservative state that has elected Republicans for decades.

Colom's victory makes him the first black person from Mississippi to be elected to the US Senate in more than 140 years.

Fewer than five thousand votes out of nearly a million counted separated him from his Republican opponent, the incumbent Cindy Hyde-Smith.

The result means the Democrats will hold 55 seats in the 100-member Senate, with a knife-edge race in Alaska still to be called.

Colom, 43, won with 49.2% of the vote, while Hyde-Smith received 48.7% and an independent candidate got 2.1%, according to figures from CBS.

Hyde-Smith congratulated Colom in a video posted on X on Wednesday evening and wished him well.

"While this was not the outcome we worked for or hoped for, I respect the decision of Mississippi voters," she said.

Colom offered a victory speech on the campus of Tougaloo College, met by hundreds of cheering supporters standing side-by-side under the night sky.

Excitement filled the air as he thanked them for the support over the days of waiting for a result since the 4 November election.

"They did not believe a moment like this was possible, but I kept the faith," Colom said.

"It's not something that I did y'all," he continued. "It's something we did."

"In Mississippi, it's local people that make the difference."

Dozens of people were gathered at the Mississippi HQ of the National Association for the Advancement of Colored People (NAACP) in Jackson on Wednesday when Colom's victory was announced.

The room burst into deafening applause and cheers.

"This is an amazing result," said Leon Russell, chairman of the NAACP board.

"This is purely the work of particularly the black community," he continued. "There was not a whole lot of money, but there was a whole lot of organising.

Across the room, filled with people embracing, Amber Thomas sat, revelling in the victory.

"When you fight, you win," Thomas said. "Right now, I am overwhelmed with joy."

The result wipes away a Republican winning streak in the Magnolia State that dates back to 1982.

The contest was never expected to be this close, with Hyde-Smith running for re-election in a state that President Donald Trump won in the 2024 election by more than 22 points.

But Democrats have scored a series of major wins in these midterm elections, taking control of both the US House of Representatives and the Senate.

The party flipped Senate seats in Republican strongholds, including Texas, South Carolina, Kansas and Iowa.

Polls suggest this was due in large part to voter frustrations with the economy and the Iran war under President Trump.

Colom appeared to a ride a national wave of resentment against Republicans.

Voter backlash against Trump's Republican party has been driven in large part by economic woes, blamed on his administration's tariffs and war with Iran, according to exit polls.

Colom, a local prosecutor, used the national mood to his advantage, highlighting his opponent's support for Trump's tariffs and giving her the nickname "Cindy High Prices".
sources.headline: Democrat Scott Colom seals historic win in Mississippi Senate race

stories.headline: Republicans push to draft Marco Rubio for 2028 after midterm losses

sources.body: A growing number of Republicans on Capitol Hill want to draft Marco Rubio for a 2028 presidential bid as they grapple with their midterms wipeout — and look beyond Vice President JD Vance. The generational losses are sparking new discussions among Hill Republicans about who should lead the party. Many argue the race to carry the mantle is now wide open — including a faction who view Rubio as a better fit, given that voters may continue to tie Vance to the president’s unpopularity, interviews with roughly two dozen GOP lawmakers reveal. “I hope he runs. I think he's the best person to communicate, to unify,” Rep. Marlin Stutzman (R-Ind.) said of Rubio in an interview. “I think he's the most talented Republican by far,” Stutzman said when asked about why he supported the secretary of State over Vance. “We're going to have to continue to re-message, put some new faces up.” The vice president still has his supporters. And he got a boost Tuesday by fellow Ohio Republican Jim Jordan being elected as the incoming House minority leader. But the election wipeout “certainly makes it harder for Vance,” said one GOP senator, who like others in this article, was granted anonymity to speak candidly. “I think Rubio is our best hope to lead Republicans out of this wilderness, and I hope he makes his break from Trump and JD early next year,” said one House Republican in the wake of the election. The openness toward Rubio — or any other candidate that’s not Vance — is a complication for the vice president, who was picked by Trump for the role that’s next in line to the presidency. Now, Vance has to grapple with being closely associated with an agenda that even GOP lawmakers argue voters harshly rebuked last week. Several lawmakers said they’ve spoken to people close to Rubio who have suggested he isn’t interested in pursuing a 2028 bid, even after Tuesday’s results. Rubio himself this week has stood by Trump’s decision to go to war against Iran and told reporters Monday he was “just not going to talk about 2028 anymore.” A person close to Rubio said the secretary of State is the only person who knows what he will do regarding a presidential bid. Right now, he’s “fully focused on doing his many jobs and isn’t thinking about 2028.” But some Hill Republicans aren’t giving up hope. “I’m a big supporter of Marco Rubio, and I’m very excited about the potential of his candidacy,” said Florida Rep. Mike Haridopolos, who has known the secretary of State for nearly three decades. “No question he’s ready to be president if he chooses to pursue the office.” “Some of us are still hoping we can draft Marco,” said another GOP senator. A State Department spokesperson declined to comment. Vance’s office didn’t respond to a request for comment. In reaction to Stutzman’s comments, a Vance ally argued that Stutzman has been one of the biggest supporters within the GOP of amnesty for unauthorized immigrants for over a decade — and that he was likely never going to support Vance, who is extremely hawkish on border security. Vance, for his part, has tried to distance himself from the unpopular Iran war, blaming it for the party’s losses in the immediate aftermath of the midterm election. His allies argue that the vice president would’ve always faced some internal opposition, like Trump did within the GOP ahead of the 2016 election. However, as the Rubio talk swirls, even some of Trump’s top MAGA allies on Capitol Hill are unwilling to publicly declare Vance the presumptive GOP nominee for 2028. “Can I skip this one?” one House GOP hardliner said. “Not wading into 2028 yet.” Some Republican senators also declined to back Vance just yet, citing their own reelections. GOP Rep. and Sen.-elect Barry Moore of Alabama said he thought Vance would certainly “have a shot” at the presidency in 2028. Moore was the first member of Congress to back Trump for the 2016 race. But Moore for now is leaving his endorsement up in the air: “We got a great bench," he said. "Whoever steps up, we'll be happy to support.” Rubio’s supporters say that he’s not as closely associated with the 2026 GOP wipeout as Vance, but he could face his own obstacles. Rubio, unlike Vance, has continued to show strong support for the war in Iran, a conflict he’s tied to as the country’s top diplomat. Some GOP lawmakers have also grown frustrated with the amount of information the Trump administration, including Rubio at times, has been willing to share about the ongoing conflict. Rubio also has his failed 2016 presidential run to contend with, including an infamous debate performance where he awkwardly repeated the same rehearsed line multiple times. One thing is clear, the 2028 presidential race is now wide open, many Hill Republicans argue as they process Tuesday’s results. And other potential candidates only appear encouraged after the midterms wipeout. Several Hill Republicans believe outgoing Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis, who has been one of the most outspoken Republicans urging a course correction after the midterms bloodbath, will get in the race as well. Sen. Josh Hawley (R-Mo.) this week also didn’t rule out a presidential bid. Sen. Ted Cruz (R-Texas) also appears likely to run. “I think everybody reserves the right to adjust. You know, learn from this,” GOP Rep. and incoming Oklahoma Sen. Kevin Hern said. Asked his favorite candidate of the three he expected to run: Vance, Rubio or DeSantis, he replied with a smile: “Everybody.” Vance does have ardent supporters, including Sen. Jim Banks of Indiana who said before the midterms he would enthusiastically back him for president in 2028. “If JD runs, he has my full support,” Banks said in an interview this week. “He continues to lead in all the polls on the Republican side to be the nominee. He's my friend. We come from the same part of the country, the same background, and he's what the country needs. I hope he runs. But I don't know if he's running or not.” Rep. Brandon Gill (R-Texas) called Vance “a friend who I’ve had the honor to work alongside. He’s the vice president, of course he’s a front-runner.” Rep. Riley Moore (R-W.Va.) said in an interview that it was the Republican “party” and not its “policies” that suffered massive losses last week. But he doesn’t blame Vance, and he supports him for the 2028 presidential race. Vance, for his part, made his own allusion to the situation he’s found himself in. "I wanted to talk, of course, about the devastating loss last week. …There are a lot of people, I think, unfairly criticizing the leader of the team … a lot of staff infighting. … And of course, there's a conversation about whether the No. 2 has what it takes to ultimately lead the team.” He finished: “I'm talking, of course, about the Ohio State Buckeyes."

stories.headline: Spanish prosecutors open investigation into child sexual abuse material on TikTok

sources.body:
Algunas de las imágenes, difuminadas, de los hallazgos de Maldita.es en TikTok

La fiscal general del Estado, Teresa Peramato, ha ordenado investigar si en la red social TikTok se han difundido miles de vídeos de abuso sexual infantil y corrupción de menores, como desveló una investigación de Maldita.es, que motivó ayer que el Gobierno haya pedido a la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) la suspensión cautelar de la actividad de la popular red social.

La fiscalía ha informado que Peramato ha designado a la fiscal de sala que coordina Criminalidad Informática, Elvira Tejada, para que estudie este caso. El inicio de esta indagación parte de una denuncia que ha presentado la Unidad de Criminalidad Informática de la propia Fiscalía General del Estado, que señala que ha tenido conocimiento relacionado “con la publicación, difusión y venta de material de abuso infantil en la plataforma TikTok”.

El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez se congratuló por las diligencias abiertas por la fiscalía mediante una publicación en la red social X. “Gran noticia: la Fiscalía acaba de abrir diligencias por la difusión de material de abuso sexual infantil en TikTok. Ya lo advertimos hace tiempo: se acabó la impunidad en las redes sociales. Ninguna plataforma está por encima de la ley. Mucho menos de los derechos de nuestros hijos e hijas”.

En el escrito se menciona uno de los aspectos destacables de la investigación periodística que ha destapado el caso. El hecho de que, supuestamente, se pueda acceder a esos contenidos ilegales desde el sistema de recomendación de la propia plataforma, de forma que se puede acceder en TikTok o en otras plataformas a “la difusión en directo de imágenes con menores de edad, mediando compensaciones de carácter económico”, como explicó el lunes Maldita.es.

La ministra de Juventud e Infancia, Sira Rego, anunció el martes después de entrevistarse con responsables de TikTok en España que había pedido al organismo regulador competente, la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD), que paralice la actividad de esta red social en España con carácter excepcional a través del mecanismo del artículo 66 del Reglamento General de Protección de Datos, que regula la eliminación de los enlaces a datos personales en internet.

La AEPD ha anunciado hoy que, después de recibir la comunicación del Ministerio de Juventud e Infancia, ha decidido solicitar a Maldita.es la relación de los enlaces que reproducen material pedófilo, requerir a TikTok información concreta sobre sus actuaciones para la retirada de los contenidos denunciados, “una vez analizada esa información, ordenar el bloqueo que impida el acceso a los enlaces y contenidos concretos y determinados que supongan un tratamiento ilícito de datos de menores”.

La agencia considera que estas decisiones suponen una medida concreta, proporcionada y adecuada, con pleno respeto a las libertades de expresión e información según la jurisprudencia internacional y nacional. Fuentes de los representantes de TikTok en España no han contestado a las preguntas formuladas por La Vanguardia  sobre este caso.
sources.headline: La Fiscalía General del Estado investiga las denuncias de abuso sexual infantil en TikTok

sources.body:
La Fiscal General del Estado, Teresa Peramato Martín , ha firmado este miércoles un decreto en el que designa a la fiscal de sala coordinadora contra la Criminalidad Informática, Elvira Tejada de la Fuente , para investigar los posibles delitos relacionados con la elaboración y difusión de contenidos de abuso sexual infantil y corrupción de menores que hubieran podido perpetrarse en la red social TikTok. Las pesquisas tienen su origen en la denuncia presentada por la entidad Maldita.es, que ha realizado una profusa investigación periodística.

En la denuncia presentada se hace constar que Maldita.es ha tenido conocimiento de actividades relacionadas con la publicación, difusión y venta de material de abuso infantil en la plataforma TikTok, así como la recomendación de contenidos de esa misma naturaleza a los que se puede acceder en la misma o en otras plataformas o la difusión en directo de imágenes con menores de edad, mediando compensaciones de carácter económico, según la Fiscalía General.

Este miércoles han comparecido los denunciantes ante la fiscal de sala coordinadora contra l a Criminalidad Informática a fin de ratificar su denuncia y presentar el material probatorio recopilado, que será objeto ahora del inmediato análisis y valoración. La investigación de Maldita.es se publicó el pasado lunes. Durante 35 días, entre el 11 de septiembre y el 15 de octubre, la fundación localizó más de mil contenidos explícitos de abuso sexual infantil , que sumaban cerca de 48 millones de visualizaciones . Cuando Maldita.es denunció una muestra de 50 vídeos, TikTok eliminó inicialmente solo cinco. El informe , el tercero que la fundación dedica al abuso sexual infantil en esta red social, identifica además más de 20.000 perfiles de potenciales pedófilos, más de 7.000 de ellos en español.

TikTok ha señalado que tan pronto se conocieron las noticias sobre los vídeos de abuso sexual infantil en su plataforma tomaron medidas para identificar y eliminar el contenido y ha indicado que trabajarán estrechamente con la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) y todas las autoridades competentes. El contenido sexualmente explícito con menores "está categóricamente prohibido" en la plataforma, ha subrayado un portavoz de la compañía.

La publicación periodística ha traído, además, una ola de reacciones. El presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, ha publicado un mensaje en la red social X en el que ha calificado la decisión de la fiscal como una “gran noticia”. “La Fiscalía acaba de abrir diligencias por la difusión de material de abuso sexual infantil en TikTok. Ya lo advertimos hace tiempo: se acabó la impunidad en las redes sociales. Ninguna plataforma está por encima de la ley. Mucho menos de los derechos de nuestros hijos e hijas”, ha escrito.

Por otra parte, la Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (AEPD) ha abierto actuaciones contra TikTok por los contenidos de abuso sexual infantil que circulan en la red social. Ha pedido a la plataforma información concreta sobre lo que está haciendo para retirarlos y ha anunciado que, una vez analizada esa información, ordenará bloquear el acceso a los enlaces .
sources.headline: La Fiscalía General ordena investigar la difusión de contenido sexual de menores en TikTok

sources.body:
La fiscal general de l'Estat ha ordenat que es posi en marxa una investigació contra la plataforma TikTok per possibles delictes relacionats amb l'elaboració i la difusió de continguts d' abús sexual infantil i corrupció de menors .

Teresa Peramato ha encarregat la feina a la fiscal de sala coordinadora contra la Criminalitat Informàtica , Elvira Tejada de la Fuente.

La investigació té l'origen en l'escrit de denúncia presentat per Maldita.es. Aquest mitjà de verificació ha detectat a TikTok més de mil vídeos d'abús sexual infantil , que superen els 48 milions de visualitzacions, i més de 20.000 perfils de pedòfils potencials que intercanvien o venen aquest tipus de material, dels quals més de 7.000 operen en espanyol.

També ha localitzat 780 comptes que utilitzen la plataforma per captar compradors de material d'abús sexual infantil , 91 emissions en directe de menors en disset països en què els usuaris demanen accions, de vegades sexuals, a canvi de diners, i una comunitat de més de 2.000 membres que busca contingut de nadons.

Els denunciants han comparegut aquest dimecres davant la fiscal de sala coordinadora contra la Criminalitat Informàtica a fi de ratificar la seva denúncia i presentar davant la Fiscalia el material probatori, que serà objecte "d'immediata anàlisi i valoració" .

Fan constar que han tingut coneixement d'activitats relacionades amb la publicació, difusió i venda de material d'abús infantil a TikTok, així com la recomanació de continguts d'aquesta mateixa naturalesa als quals es pot accedir tant en aquesta xarxa social com en altres plataformes . També fan constar la difusió en directe d'imatges amb menors d'edat, mitjançant compensacions.

Paral·lelament, l'Agència Espanyola de Protecció de Dades ha anunciat que demanarà a TikTok informació concreta sobre les actuacions que té en marxa per retirar aquests continguts.

L'agència alerta, però, que no té competències per tancar l'aplicació , com havia demanat el govern espanyol. El Ministeri de Joventut i Infància també va enviar un escrit a la Fiscalia per sol·licitar que posés en marxa una investigació.

El president del govern espanyol, Pedro Sánchez , ha celebrat la decisió de la Fiscalia i ha dit que "s'ha acabat la impunitat a les xarxes socials". "Cap plataforma està per sobre de la llei. Molt menys dels drets dels nostres fills i filles", assegura en una publicació a X .
sources.headline: La Fiscalia investiga TikTok arran de la denúncia que hi ha més de mil vídeos d'abús sexual infantil

stories.headline: Spanish government challenges Valencia's 'national priority' policy in the Constitutional Court

sources.body:
El Consell de Ministres interposarà un recurs d'inconstitucionalitat contra la llei d'acompanyament als pressupostos de la Generalitat Valenciana .

La norma, aprovada al juliol pel PP i Vox, incorpora el principi de "prioritat nacional" en l'accés a l'habitatge i prestacions socials.

Una màxima que, segons el criteri de La Moncloa, contradiu "condicions bàsiques com la igualtat entre persones", tal com ha assenyalat aquest dimarts la portaveu del govern espanyol, Elma Saiz, durant la roda de premsa posterior al Consell de Ministres.

Concretament, el concepte de la "prioritat nacional" se sustenta en la idea que els espanyols han de tenir prioritat en el repartiment d'ajudes o l'accés a habitatge protegit.

Una idea que recorda molt l'"Amèrica primer" de Trump o "Les français d'abord" de Jean-Marie Le Pen i que ha marcat, a banda del pacte entre el PP i Vox a València, també els acords de les dues formacions a l'Aragó i Extremadura .

Aquest, però, no és l'únic concepte problemàtic que conté la llei, segons l'executiu. Dels 200 articles que componen la llei d'acompanyament als pressupostos valencians, els socialistes en volen impugnar una vintena , que tracten qüestions com la prioritat de la reagrupació familiar dels menors d'edat tutelats i la prohibició de l'ús del burca o el nicab en espais públics.

Així mateix, també es reclama al Tribunal Constitucional que revisi articles lligats amb la igualtat de les persones LGTBI en l'àmbit educatiu o amb la "protecció del dret a la vida dels no nascuts".
sources.headline: La Moncloa porta al Constitucional el principi de "prioritat nacional" de la Generalitat Valenciana

stories.headline: Around 50 arrested in Barcelona unrest after housing demonstration

sources.body:
Una cinquantena de persones han estat detingudes a Barcelona, segons l'Ajuntament, arran dels aldarulls que hi ha hagut un cop desconvocada la manifestació unitària per la vaga general .

Els incidents s'han produït als entorns de la plaça Catalunya, el passeig de Gràcia i el carrer Pelai .

En aquesta zona, un grup de joves encaputxats ha fet trencadissa de vidres en aparadors de diversos comerços –alguns dels quals s'havien protegit– i ha cremat escombraries, contenidors i mobiliari urbà.

Els Mossos han disparat projectils de foam , fent-ne un "ús selectiu", segons el cos policial. A hores d'ara es manté a la zona un fort desplegament dels Mossos d'Esquadra .

L'alcalde de la ciutat, Jaume Collboni, ha condemnat els fets amb rotunditat : "Aquesta no és la manera d'expressar una posició política", ha dit.

Segons Collboni, la jornada de vaga s'ha desenvolupat amb normalitat, però "grups violents i organitzats s'han infiltrat" a la manifestació i, un cop acabada, han protagonitzat els actes violents. L'alcalde ha xifrat entre sis i deu els comerços afectats pel vandalisme, i els ha expressat el seu suport.

Per la seva banda, el president de la Generalitat ha advertit a través de la xarxa X que "a Catalunya, qui la fa la paga" .

Salvador Illa assegura que "ni la violència ni el vandalisme representen les persones que s'han manifestat pacíficament avui durant tota la jornada", i transmet "tot el suport" als Mossos i "la resta de cossos de seguretat que treballen per restablir l'ordre i la convivència":

La protesta és legítima; la violència, no.

En un sentit similar s'ha expressat la consellera d'Interior, que, com Illa, ha recordat que "a Catalunya, qui la fa la paga". Núria Parlon –també a la xarxa X – ha dit que "manifestar-se és un dret", però " la violència i els aldarulls, una línia vermella ". La consellera, a més, ha mostrat "tot el suport" als Mossos, la Guàrdia Urbana i els Bombers per "protegir la convivència i restablir la calma".

Al centre de la ciutat, alguns veïns també han sortit al carrer per queixar-se dels actes vandàlics i intentar-los impedir.

Els manifestants s'han mogut per la plaça Catalunya, la Rambla, el carrer Balmes i la plaça Universitat, i després s'han traslladat cap a la zona del carrer Diputació.

A la zona, molts aparadors han acabat trencats o bé pintats. Moments abans d'aquests incidents ja s'havia vist llançament d'objectes i material pirotècnic contra la línia policial.

Aparadors trencats i aldarulls a la zona del passeig de Gràcia de Barcelona, després que s'hagi desconvocat la manifestació https://t.co/j0LRrx06gV https://t.co/TTrWw73kWA

L'aparició de cop i volta dels efectius de seguretat un cop els convocants han confirmat el final definitiu de la concentració de la tarda ha provocat moments de cridòria i els primers enfrontaments .
sources.headline: Prop de 50 detinguts a Barcelona pels aldarulls després de la manifestació de la vaga general

sources.body:
El alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, durante su intervención en la mesa redonda de alcaldes del HOWS Barcelona 2026 / ACN

El alcalde de Barcelona, Jaume Collboni, ha condenado los "actos vandálicos" protagonizados por "grupos violentos, organizados e infiltrados" que se han registrado al término de las manifestaciones celebradas en el centro de la ciudad con ocasión de la huelga general y ha cifrado en 50 el número de detenidos.

En declaraciones a la prensa desde el centro de emergencias de Barcelona, que reúne a los cuerpos policiales, de bomberos y sanitarios, Collboni ha condenado "con toda rotundidad" estos actos vandálicos registrados tras una jornada de huelga general que había transcurrido "con normalidad con carácter general" y al finalizar una gran manifestación que ha transcurrido "de manera pacífica".

El alcalde barcelonés ha informado de que los incidentes se han saldado con 50 detenidos, pese a que los Mossos d'Esquadra habían cifrado las detenciones en 18 en su último balance.

Collboni ha expresado su "repulsa por los ataques a bienes públicos y privados" durante los disturbios y ha transmitido su apoyo a los comerciantes afectados.

Ha indicado también que los incidentes han quedado circunscritos a pocas zonas del centro de Barcelona, donde se han quemado numerosos contenedores a pesar de que el Ayuntamiento había retirado preventivamente casi un centenar, y que entre seis y diez comercios han sido vandalizados, casi todos ellos de grandes cadenas.

Ha querido reconocer la actuación de las fuerzas de seguridad y ha reiterado que "en Barcelona, quien la hace la paga", por lo que el Ayuntamiento pedirá indemnizaciones a las personas que los jueces consideren culpables de estos actos vandálicos.

El centro de la ciudad de Barcelona ha recuperado ya la normalidad, a la que ha contribuido también una fuerte lluvia que ha empezado a caer pasadas las 22:30 horas.
sources.headline: Collboni condena los actos vandálicos en Barcelona y cifra en 50 el número de detenidos

sources.body:
Tras una manifestación en favor del derecho a la vivienda multitudinaria, familiar y pacífica, decenas de jóvenes encapuchados han empezado a protagonizar, pasadas las siete y media de la tarde, los primeros disturbios en la confluencia de Gran Via con paseo de Gràcia, en Barcelona. Los convocados han reventado persianas de comercios de la zona como Victoria's Secret, H&M y Geox . Del primero han salido con ropa y han encendido un fuego frente a la tienda, escena que se ha repetido ante el local de Apple . De hecho, las hogueras, las barricadas, la rotura de escaparates y el lanzamiento de piedras, contestados con cargas policiales y proyectiles de foam, han marcado la batalla campal al final de la jornada de huelga en el centro de la ciudad. Pasadas las nueve de la noche, los Mossos habían detenido a 18 personas por altercados.

Disturbios tras las manifestaciones por la huelga general en Barcelona / Alejandro García / EFE

Los enfrentamientos se han producido cuando la protesta ya había llegado al entorno de la plaza de Catalunya, donde algunos manifestantes han empezado a lanzar artefactos pirotécnicos, como cohetes y fuertes petardos , contra los agentes de los Mossos d'Esquadra desplegados en la zona. Ante estos incidentes, la policía catalana ha desencochado y, a pie, ha abierto una linea policial para desplazar a los manifestantes hacia la plaza de Catalunya.

La tensión ha ido aumentando y los agentes se han desplegado y han advertido de que se disponían a cargar. El dispositivo ha ido avanzando y los manifestantes se han dispersado hacia la calle de Pelai , donde se han registrado carreras entre los jóvenes y la policía. Precisamente en esa calle, tocando a la plaza de la Universitat, ha habido las primeras cargas policiales ante el lanzamiento de pintura, piedras y botellas por parte de los jóvenes, que también han levantado barricadas con contenedores en llamas. La policía también ha dispersado a los manifestantes con lanzamiento de proyectiles de foam. Cerca de las nueve de la noche, los disturbios ya eran menos intensos y con focos más dispersos, aunque aún activos.

Ante los altercados, el president de la Generalitat, Salvador Illa , ha condenado los hechos en X. "Ni la violencia ni el vandalismo representan a las personas que se han manifestado pacíficamente hoy durante toda la jornada", ha dicho Illa. "En Catalunya, 'qui la fa la paga'", ha asegurado el presidente, que ha dado "todo el apoyo a los Mossos y al resto de los cuerpos de seguridad que trabajan para restablecer el orden y la convivencia".

Ya durante la marcha, grupos de encapuchados muy jóvenes habían realizado pintadas, de forma organizada, en algunas de las principales tiendas del paseo de Gràcia. Mientras unos pintaban, otros vigilaban para que ni policía ni los numerosos medios de comunicación presentes en la avenida se acercasen a ellos.

La tensión ha ido aumentando a lo largo de la jornada. De hecho, la mañana se ha saldado sin incidentes graves. Sin embargo, pocas horas antes de iniciarse las manifestaciones de la tarde, se han empezado a registrar algunas protestas más contundentes . Piquetes con personas encapuchadas han obligado a cerrar algunos comercios del centro, principalmente de restauración. En algunos se han vivido momentos de tensión, como ha sido el caso de varios locales de comida rápida de la plaza de Urquinaona donde se han realizado pintadas en paredes y cristales, se han pegado adhesivos, se han roto vasos y platos, y se ha intentado quemar mobiliario del local.
sources.headline: Jóvenes encapuchados provocan disturbios en Barcelona al final de una manifestación por la vivienda masiva y familiar

sources.body:
Clashes have broken out between groups of masked men and police in Barcelona after tens of thousands of people took part in Spain's first general strike for 14 years, called by the country's main unions over housing and the high cost of living.

Some 120,000 people joined a demonstration in the capital Madrid and more than 50,000 turned out in Barcelona, where footage showed masked men setting fire to rubbish bins and smashing shop windows as police fired tear gas.

Transport and other public services across Spain faced serious disruption.

Spaniards are due to vote in parliamentary elections on 29 November.

The head of the big UGT labour union, Pepe Álvarez, said the strike was a success with "massive" participation, while Unai Sordo of the CC OO union said turnout was "very significant."

There was a heavy police presence in the centre of Barcelona on Wednesday evening, with officers wearing helmets and riot shields.

Some of the disturbances took place in the Passeig de Gràcia, close to the iconic Plaça de Catalunya in the centre of the city.

Small fires burned in the middle of the streets as bins were set alight. Local media reported that a group of people fired fireworks towards police and looted shops including the Lego store. Protesters were also seen trying to enter the Apple Store.

The BBC spoke to a woman who attended the protests in Barcelona who said it was mostly very peaceful and "joyful". She said she was there to protest about the housing costs and that "there were a lot of children and old people there."

She was in the area of Las Ramblas in the evening and saw fires in the streets. "The fires were everywhere, it was very intense," she said.

Earlier in the day there was major disruption around Madrid and Barcelona, with traffic halted on several main roads.

The interior ministry said dozens of people were arrested for a variety of incidents and Spanish reports said estate agencies had seen attacks on their offices.

"We've completely brought the city to a standstill," a protester in Madrid told Reuters news agency, adding there was widespread support for the general strike. "Everyone's out there, despite the rainy weather; everyone's out on the streets."

Another protester, 37-year-old teacher Olga Domingo, said she was protesting because "the housing situation is outrageous. The current cost of living compared to wages is completely unsustainable".

The strike was triggered by widespread protests over affordable housing and rising living costs, after the eviction of 87-year-old Maricarmen Abascal from a flat in Madrid where she had lived for seven decades. She died in hospital weeks later.

Rental prices in the capital have risen in recent years. The monthly cost of a 50 sq m apartment in Madrid was an average of €1,170 ($1,300; £1,000) in October, according to property portal Idealista, while Spain's average gross monthly salary is about €2,460.

That amounts to nearly half the average gross salary, well above the 30% level of affordability often recommended by housing experts and public institutions.
sources.headline: Clashes erupt in Barcelona after thousands join Spain general strike

sources.body: El pas de la borrasca Charles continuarà condicionant el temps de Catalunya durant les pròximes hores. stories.headline: Octavi Vilà named to succeed Omella as archbishop of Barcelona

sources.body:
L'actual bisbe de Girona , Octavi Vilà, substituirà el cardenal Joan Josep Omella i Omella al capdavant de l' arquebisbat de Barcelona , que deixarà el càrrec i es retirarà a Saragossa.

El Vaticà ho ha anunciat aquest dimecres, coincidint amb la vaga general per l'habitatge, després de cinc anys d'espera i molta expectació entre els fidels catòlics. Es dona la circumstància que els bisbes estan obligats a jubilar-se als 75 anys, però Omella ja n'ha fet 80.

Octavi Vilà assumeix l'arquebisbat quan fa només dos anys que es va convertir en bisbe de Girona .

Nascut a Tarragona el desembre del 1961 , Octavi Vilà és monjo cistercenc i el 2005 va entrar al monestir de Poblet , on va exercir d'abat entre el 2015 i el 2024. Durant aquesta etapa, va presidir la Congregació Cistercenca de la Corona d'Aragó i la Reunió d'Abats i Provincials (RAP) de Catalunya. També va formar part del Capítol General i del Sínode de l'Orde Cistercenc.

Actualment és membre de la Comissió Episcopal per a la Vida Consagrada de la Conferència Episcopal Espanyola i presideix la Comissió Interdiocesana de Litúrgia de la Conferència Episcopal Tarraconense.

El futur arquebisbe és llicenciat en Geografia i Història (1984) i diplomat en Biblioteconomia i Documentació (1987) per la Universitat de Barcelona. També ha cursat un postgrau en Noves Tecnologies de la Informació per la Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya (1996) i un en Gestió Cultural per la Universitat Pompeu Fabra (2000). A més, entre el 2007 i el 2015 va estudiar Filosofia i Teologia i la llicència en Teologia Sistemàtica a la Facultat de Teologia de Catalunya.
sources.headline: Octavi Vilà serà el pròxim arquebisbe de Barcelona en substitució de Joan Josep Omella

sources.body:
La Santa Sede ha hecho hoy oficial al mediodía el nombramiento del sucesor del arzobispo de Barcelona, el cardenal Juan José Omella. Quien tomará el testigo es el actual obispo de Girona, el cisterciense Octavi Vilà, puesto que a la misma hora se ha convocado hoy una rueda de prensa en ambas diócesis. Lo habitual en estos casos, más allá del nombramiento que sale en los documentos del Vaticano a las 12:00 horas, es que se cite a los medios a la misma hora en la diócesis del obispo elegido y en la diócesis del prelado saliente.

Desde hacía semanas había rumrum en los mentideros eclesiásticos sobre quién podía ser el sucesor de Omella, puesto que estaba ya fuera de plazo desde abril. Al cumplir 80 años suele expirar la prórroga que se concede a los obispos, que están obligados a presentar su renuncia al Papa cuando cumplen los 75 por el derecho canónico. Vilà, de 65 años, tiene al menos diez años por delante en la capital catalana.

Con todo, con la visita de León XVI a Barcelona del pasado mes de junio ya se dio por hecho que la cuestión sucesoria se demoraría como mínimo hasta el verano y en las últimas semanas se habían disparado las especulaciones y los rumores, puesto que desde septiembre se decía que ya se había firmado el nombre del sucesor y que el anuncio era inminente. En todo caso, aún pasarán unas semanas hasta que Vilà tome posesión de su nueva diócesis. Por ahora se sabe que será el próximo 19 de diciembre cuando inicie su ministerio, justo antes de Navidad, en la Sagrada Família. Se ha escogido la basílica porque la catedral está en obras. Con todo, será en la catedral donde tome posesión, en una fecha todavía por determinar. Quizá será el día 18 de diciembre o quizá el día 19 a primera hora.

Al final, el nombramiento llega a las puertas de la campaña electoral de los comicios del 29-N, y coincide con un día de huelga general, lo que demuestra una vez más que el Vaticano maneja sus propios tiempos y que su agenda no siempre coincide con la de otras instituciones de la esfera pública. Además, el anuncio del nuevo obispo llega durante un viaje apostólico del Papa a América Latina. La Santa Sede procura no interferir en asuntos públicos, y cuando se convocan elecciones en un país donde el Papa tiene que viajar se suele suspender el viaje. Con los nombramientos episcopales opera otra lógica, ya que en Brasil, hace unas semanas, ya se vio como durante la campaña se nombraba a varios obispos.

Pese a estar próxima su sucesión, en estas últimas semanas Omella se había mostrado muy activo. En verano intervino algunas fundaciones que dependen del arzobispado , al detectar presuntas irregularidades, y hace apenas unas semanas firmó un decreto para que haya más transparencia para aquellas personas sometidas a la jurisdicción episcopal.

Vilà no es un nombre ajeno a las quinielas de la sucesión. Se había señalado en medios especializados que podía ser el elegido, si bien nadie, ante cuestiones de ámbito eclesiástico, se atreve a dar nada por seguro mientras no lleve el membrete de Roma. Con todo, es uno de los que irrumpió en la recta final, puesto que nadie le situaba como caballo ganador hace unos meses.
sources.headline: Octavi Vilà reemplazará a Omella como arzobispo de Barcelona

sources.body:
El papa León XIV ya tiene sustituto para Juan José Omella , el hasta ahora arzobispo de Barcelona. Será Octavi Vilà, el actual obispo de Girona . Lo ha anunciado este miércoles a través del boletín oficial del Vaticano. De este modo el Pontífice, buen conocedor de Catalunya, opta por un perfil marcadamente catalanista . Vilà ( Tarragona, 1961 ), antiguo abad de Poblet , de talante conciliador, destaca por su defensa del diálogo, su sensibilidad social y su apuesta por una Iglesia más abierta y cercana a los fieles. Llevaba dos años y ocho meses al frente del obispado gerundense.

De la vida contemplativa en Poblet a los despachos del arzobispado de Barcelona. Fray Octavi Vilà ha recorrido un camino que difícilmente habría imaginado cuando, a los 43 años, dejó atrás más de dos décadas de trabajo en la Hemeroteca de Tarragona para ingresar en el monasterio cisterciense. Licenciado en Geografía e Historia y diplomado en Biblioteconomía y Documentación por la Universitat de Barcelona, en 2005 decidió abrazar la vocación monástica. Aquella decisión, sin embargo, acabó llevándolo a asumir responsabilidades de cada vez mayor envergadura: en 2015, los monjes de Poblet lo eligieron abad; en 2024, el papa Francisco lo nombró obispo de Girona; y ahora, León XIV lo ha escogido para suceder a Joan Josep Omella al frente del arzobispado de Barcelona.

Su vinculación con Poblet , sin embargo, había comenzado antes de vestir el hábito. Entre 2000 y 2005 fue secretario de la Hermandad del monasterio y uno de los colaboradores más estrechos del abad Josep Alegre, con quien trabajó para acercar a los laicos a la vida y la espiritualidad cisterciense. Vilà participó en la renovación de la entidad, que impulsó actividades de oración, retiros y encuentros con intelectuales y profesionales católicos.

Octavi Vilà asume el cargo de arzobispo de Barcelona. / Bisbat Girona

En 2015 sucedió a Alegre como abad y, durante casi nueve años, compaginó el gobierno de la comunidad con la gestión del patrimonio cultural, la presidencia del Patronato del Archivo Montserrat Tarradellas i Macià y las responsabilidades vinculadas a las comunidades cistercienses femeninas. Una experiencia que le permitió conocer el funcionamiento de la Iglesia más allá de los muros de Poblet. "Lo que me gustaba era ser monje; ser abad también fue un encargo que la comunidad me pidió y lo acepté, pero uno no nace con vocación de abad o de obispo", explicaba el pasado mayo en una entrevista al Diari de Girona .

En enero de 2024 falleció Josep Alegre, uno de los principales referentes de Vilà en Poblet, que también mantenía una estrecha amistad con el cardenal Joan Josep Omella. Apenas diez días después de la muerte de Alegre, el 5 de febrero, Vilà recibió dos llamadas de la nunciatura apostólica que acabarían llevándolo al Obispado de Girona . Necesitó cinco días para reflexionar y aceptar el encargo, después de consultarlo con su director espiritual y el arzobispo de Tarragona, Joan Planellas . Sus dudas no tenían nada que ver con Girona, sino con el hecho de tener que abandonar la comunidad que había elegido. "Me daba cierto reparo pasar de la vida comunitaria a una vida más solitaria", reconocía en marzo de 2024 en una entrevista a este diario, pocos días después de ser nombrado obispo de Girona. Finalmente, el 21 de abril fue ordenado obispo en la Catedral de Girona, convirtiéndose en el primer monje que asumía el gobierno de la diócesis en casi seis siglos.
sources.headline: Octavi Vilà, el arzobispo catalanista y conciliador que solo quería ser monje
